title: On-call and incident response playbook — comprehensive
author: Ava Thompson
content:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standard operating procedures for on-call rotations, incident detection & triage, runbook execution, postmortem process, game days, and customer/status-page communications. It is the canonical reference for SREs, engineers, and incident commanders responsible for keeping inference services available and meeting our SLOs.

Scope
Applies to all production-facing services (example services: inference-api, request-router, model-cache, kv-cache, batcher, telemetry-ingest). Non-production incidents should follow the lighter-weight dev/test incident process documented in the /eng-platform/runbooks page.

Incident severity & definitions
- Sev0 (P0 / Critical): Customer-facing outage causing system-wide unavailability or data loss (e.g., inference-api returns 5xx for >50% requests for >5 minutes). Requires immediate page and incident commander.
- Sev1 (P1 / Major): Major degradation impacting significant customer traffic (e.g., latency >2x SLO for >10% of traffic for 10+ minutes).
- Sev2 (P2 / Minor): Functional impact to subset of users or degraded non-critical functionality (e.g., embeddings delayed for a region).
- Sev3 (P3 / Low): Internal issues, maintenance, or informational alerts (no customer impact).

SLO / alerting thresholds (examples)
| Service | Availability SLO | Alert threshold | Primary metric |
| inference-api | 99.95% monthly | 5xx rate >0.5% over 10m | 5xx count / total |
| request-router | 99.99% | 95th latency >500ms over 5m | p95 latency |
| model-cache | 99.9% | cache miss rate >10% over 15m | miss_count / requests |

Alerting & tooling
- PagerDuty: primary paging system for on-call rotations.
- Slack: incident channel (#incidents/<incident-id>) used for coordination and action logs.
- Statuspage (customer-facing) for incident messages and updates.
- Internal runbook repo: internal_runbooks (link in related_pages).
- Observability: Datadog (metrics/dashboards), Honeycomb (traces), Loki (logs).

Ownership & roles
- Incident Commander (IC): overall decision maker for the incident; organizes comms, triage, and postmortem. Typically the most senior on-call for the affected service.
- Primary on-call engineer: first responder; executes runbook steps, collects diagnostics, and escalates to IC if needed.
- Secondary on-call (backup): assists and takes over if primary is off-shift.
- Platform SRE: responsible for infra-level issues (networking, cloud APIs, GPU-fleet).
- Communications lead: drafts status page and customer/partner messages.

Escalation matrix (example)
1) PagerDuty page -> primary on-call (5 min to acknowledge).
2) If not acknowledged in 5 min -> secondary on-call.
3) If unresolved in 15 min -> paging the IC and on-call lead.
4) If incident hits Sev0 -> executive pager and incident war room (video + Slack) invoked.

Initial triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
1. Acknowledge the page and join #incidents/<id>.
2. Record start time and severity in the incident header.
3. Determine blast radius (which services, regions, customers).
4. Gather telemetry: top errors, p95/p99 latency, deployment events, recent config changes.
5. Apply quick mitigations if available (e.g., failover to replica, scale up batchers, revert last deploy).
6. If recovery not immediate, escalate to IC and open a statuspage draft.

Runbook template (use for all production services)
- Runbook title: <service> - <symptom>
- Purpose: short description of the runbook intent.
- When to run: trigger conditions (metrics/alerts).
- Prereqs: IAM/credentials, access to project, runbook owner.
- Safe-mode checklist: steps that are low-risk and often resolve issues.
- Diagnostic steps: list of commands/dashboards and expected outputs.
- Mitigation steps: ordered steps to reduce customer impact.
- Rollback steps: how to revert last deploy/config change.
- Post-exec verification: checks to confirm recovery.
- Owner & escalation contact: primary, secondary, IC.

Runbook example: inference-api high 5xx rate
Purpose: Restore successful request rate for inference-api when 5xx rate spikes >0.5% sustained over 10m.
When to run: PagerDuty alert: inference-api-5xx-high.
Prereqs: kubectl access to prod-cluster, PagerDuty & Slack.
Safe-mode checklist:
- Check recent deploys: `git log --oneline -n 5` and Datadog deployment markers.
- Scale replicas: `kubectl scale deploy inference-api --replicas=4 -n prod` (if <4).
- Enable cached responses: set ENV CACHE_READ_ONLY=true to reduce model load.
Diagnostics:
1. Top error logs: `kubectl logs -l app=inference-api -n prod --tail 200 | grep ERROR | head -n 50`
2. Check model-server health: `curl -fsS http://model-server.health/health`
3. Inspect p95 latency: Datadog > inference-api > latency (time window 10m).
Mitigations:
1. If a bad deploy is suspected: rollback to previous image tag: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/inference-api -n prod` and monitor p95/p99.
2. If an upstream model is slow: divert traffic to model-variant B via request-router feature flag.
3. If GPU nodes are overloaded: drain and cordon noisy nodes and scale up capacity via autoscaler.
Post-exec verification:
- 5xx rate <0.2% sustained for 10 minutes; p95 latency below threshold; no increase in error logs for 15 minutes.

Postmortem process & template
- Postmortem must be opened for any Sev0/Sev1 incident or any incident that triggers customer-facing communication.
- Timeline: create draft within 24 hours, owner assigned. Final postmortem published within 5 business days.
- Blameless language required. Focus on contributing factors and systemic fixes.
Postmortem template (use file name pattern: postmortem-<service>-YYYYMMDD-<short-title>.md)
- Title
- Incident summary (one-paragraph)
- Timeline (timestamped events)
- Impact (customers affected, duration, SLO impact)
- Root cause analysis (RCA)
- Contributing factors
- Actions & owners (with due dates)
- Follow-up & preventative measures
- Severity/classification & lessons learned

On-call rotations & policies
- Rotation model: primary + secondary weekly rotations. Shifts start Monday 08:00 UTC to next Monday 08:00 UTC.
- Handover: outgoing on-call must publish a short handover note in #oncall-handoffs in the last 2 hours of shift (active incidents, ongoing mitigations, capacity events).
- Time-off & swaps: use the on-call calendar (link in related_pages) to request swaps. Swaps must be acknowledged by both participants and an admin.
- Overnight policy: for engineers in the US, minimal overnight pager tasks are delegated to SRE night team; escalation follows standard matrix.
- On-call compensation & expectations: see /company-handbook/03_benefits-and-perks for details.

Game days & training
- Frequency: quarterly service-level game days + annual company-wide disaster recovery exercise.
- Objectives: validate runbooks, test failover, exercise communications & postmortem cadence.
- Typical agenda (4 hours):
  1. Kickoff & goals (15m)
  2. Scenario briefing (10m)
  3. Execution: simulate outage and runbooks (120m)
  4. Debrief & capture action items (45m)
  5. Postmortem write-up assignment (30m)
- Post-game-day: publish findings and track actions in the reliability-initiatives board.

Status page and customer communications templates
- Statuspage policy: all customer-facing incidents must have a status page entry within 30 minutes of confirmed customer impact. Subsequent updates every 30–60 minutes until resolved, then a complete post-incident update within 24 hours.
- Status page template (short):
  - Title: Partial outage – inference API (region)
  - Impact: Customers may experience failed requests or increased latency.
  - Status: Identified / Monitoring / Resolved
  - Started: <UTC timestamp>
  - Update: <short summary of mitigation taken>
  - Next update: <ETA>

- Customer email / support message template (for customer-success and accounts):
  Subject: Incident: Partial outage impacting inference API – <date>

  Hello <customer-name>,

  We’re writing to inform you of a partial outage that began at <UTC time>. Impact: some requests to the inference API in <region> experienced increased failure rates / latency.

  What we’re doing: Our on-call team identified the root cause (brief description) and applied mitigations (e.g., rollback, traffic diversion). We will follow up with a detailed post-incident report within 24 hours.

  If you have concerns or require a dedicated postmortem, reply to this message and we’ll prioritize follow-up.

  — Redwood Inference Operations

Templates for Slack public incident channel messages
- Initial page message:
  [INC-<id>] Sev1: inference-api 5xx spike. Acknowledged by @<name>. IC: @<name>. Joining channel.
- Status update example:
  [INC-<id>] 12:18 UTC – Mitigation applied: rolled back inference-api to tag v1.2.3. Observing p95 dropping from 420ms → 190ms. Monitoring.
- Final resolve message:
  [INC-<id>] 12:55 UTC – Incident resolved. Root cause: bad inference-model release; action: pin model-variant and improve pre-deploy perf test. Postmortem: link.

Communication ownership & approval
- Communications lead drafts statuspage & customer messages. IC approves operational details. Head of Customer Success approves customer-facing emails for enterprise customers.

Retention & incident artifacts
- All incident channels must include an action-tracked meeting note and link to the postmortem doc.
- Checklist to close incident: incident timeline complete, diagnostics attached, actions created with owners and due dates, statuspage final update posted, postmortem assigned.

Continuous improvement & metrics
- KPIs tracked monthly by eng-sre: mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), mean time to mitigate (MTTM), mean time to recover (MTTR), number of Sev1/Sev0 incidents, percentage of postmortems with action items closed within 30 days.

Appendices
A. Quick commands & dashboards
- Datadog dashboards: inference-api -> https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/redwood/inference-api
- Common kubectl commands: `kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=inference-api`
- Model-serving health endpoints: `/health`, `/metrics`, `/status`

B. Contact table
| Role | Pager | Slack handle | Backup |
| Incident Commander | pager: IC-pager | @ic-oncall | eng-oncall-lead |
| Primary on-call | pager: primary | @oncall-engineer | @secondary-oncall |

C. Incident playbook checklist (short)
1. Page and acknowledge (5m). 2. Triage & gather telemetry (10m). 3. Apply safe mitigations (20m). 4. Escalate & open statuspage (30m). 5. Recover & verify (60m). 6. Postmortem draft (24h).

D. Example action items (from previous incidents)
- Implement pre-deploy perf check for model packaging (owner: Morgan Liu, due: 2026-04-15).
- Add automated rollback on model-variant performance regression (owner: Diego Martinez, due: 2026-05-01).

E. References
- SLOs & error budgets: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets
- Runbook templates: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks
- On-call rotations calendar: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/oncall-and-incident-response-process-and-rotations-2026.json

If you have feedback or suggested edits to this playbook please open a PR on the internal doc repo or ping the eng-sre channel.
